A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the `mammal/eukaryotic loop' in NATs has a significant impact on the binding mode of the cofactor, and that this loop is a key element in determining the mode of binding.
the mode of cofactor binding in NAT enzymes depends on the structural constraints imposed by the insertion loop.
the mode of CoA recognition in NATs is more conserved among orthologous NAT proteins than previously thought, with the exception of the NAT1s from M. marinum and M. loti.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mode of cofactor binding by NATs is highly conserved among orthologous NAT enzymes, which has implications in the rational design of inhibitors of this family of enzymes.
the mode of CoA binding is not a defining feature of NATs, and that the mode of cofactor binding should not be used to discriminate between NATs.
the `mammal/eukaryotic loop' is not required for the recognition of CoA by NATs, as the mode of binding in (RHILOT)NAT1 is very similar to that of the loopless M. marinum ortholog.
